warden_oil.title: Keep the lantern lit
warden_oil.body: Oil refills slowly. Burn nearby corpses with 3 or Right-click to reclaim 20 oil per body and leave fire behind. Your lantern cone strips Shrouded and stuns wraiths; plant a ward to protect allies.

monk_beat.title: Hear the beat
monk_beat.body: Resonance rises with hits and fades after a quiet moment. The resource orb pulses every 1.2 seconds: strike within the pulse for extra damage and Resonance. Toll spends 25 Resonance to stun; Sound the Corpse makes nearby Tolls stronger.

witch_offal.title: Feed the crows
witch_offal.body: Offal comes from corpses. Harvest one with 1 to gain 30 Offal and summon pecking crows. Butcher a body with Right-click to leave three healing charms for allies.

veil_forms.title: Walk the Veil
veil_forms.body: <kbd>1</kbd> changes form. Veil form drains your meter and protects you from enemy attacks while you move faster; your spirit attacks deal less damage. Life form refills Veil. Lay a body to rest for healing and echo corpses, then raise or cross to an echo.

reaper_souls.title: Fill the soul bag
reaper_souls.body: You are the Reaper: green energy refills on its own, so keep swinging and keep moving. Every kill sends its soul to your soul bag (the skull bar): each soul adds 2% damage. 2 Reap, 3 Wraith Walk and 4 Soul Burst spend souls for much more. 1 throws the scythe to spin on a pack.

minimap.title: Choose your path
minimap.body: Click a walkable spot on the minimap to travel there. The amber marker shows your fixed destination. Click another spot to change it; sealed halls stay closed. Hover a spell icon for its cost, targeting, effects and a useful combat tip.

auto_combat.title: Settle into the fight
auto_combat.body: On Easy, auto combat engages enemies in the current area, uses equipped rites and may cast your signature when useful. It drinks healing flasks and mends you while under attack. It steps out of boss telegraphs (rings, cones, spokes, burning ground) and hostile pools on its own, then carries on attacking. The Hollow Knight also guards automatically. Click or use movement keys to take control. Toggle it with <kbd>G</kbd> or the Auto button.

knight_rage.title: Rage, not essence
knight_rage.body: You are the Hollow Knight: no thralls, no Grave Essence. Rage builds when you are hit, when LMB Hollow Cut catches a body, and fastest of all from a perfect block — hold 3 Bulwark facing the blow. Spend it on 2 Grave Slam. 4 Corpse Vigil is your only heal, so keep a body spare.

change_class.title: A new discipline
change_class.body: Choose a class here whenever you want. Your level, gold, items and permanent progress stay with the same character. Changing discipline returns you safely to the Chapterhouse with its new model and passives.

welcome.title: Take your time
welcome.body: This gathering sanctuary has no enemies. Click a tree, ore seam, pool or grave to work it (P shows your Skills), or walk on whenever you like. Move with WASD or by clicking the ground. The Next line under the minimap offers one optional suggestion at a time. Esc opens Settings.

move.title: Walk among the dead
move.body: Aim with the mouse and <kbd>Click</kbd> an enemy for your basic attack; <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Click</kbd> attacks without moving. Press <kbd>1</kbd>–<kbd>4</kbd> for rites and <kbd>Right-click</kbd> (or <kbd>5</kbd>) for your fifth. Watch the ground for warning rings and step out of them.

exhume.title: A corpse lies near
exhume.body: Press {key:exhume} to Exhume the corpse nearest your cursor and raise it as your thrall. Unclaimed bodies rot away.

wave.title: Wave Speed
wave.body: You can afford to Quicken the waves (lower right). Faster waves bring more dead and richer rewards. The three diamonds are milestones (tiers 3, 6 and 8) that add wave affixes; hover them. Use − to dial the active tier back down whenever the pressure is too much.

deacon.title: Kill the Crypt Deacon first
deacon.body: Deacons steal unclaimed corpses and raise them as Risen against you. Watch for the green beam, and put it down before it reaches the dead.

gate.title: A sealed door
gate.body: This gate stays sealed until you have slain enough of the dead on this side. The count sits under the map, top right.

essence.title: Grave Essence
essence.body: Rites cost essence (the blue orb). Bone Needle is free, and every needle hit refunds some, so keep a target under attack between rites.

thrall.title: Your first thrall
thrall.body: It follows you and fights what you fight. Raise more with {key:exhume} up to your cap (the skull count, lower right); past the cap your oldest crumbles. A corpse remembers what it was: Penitents rise as archers, Deacons as bone mages, Carrion Sacs as plague bearers.

litany.title: Black Litany
litany.body: Press {key:black_litany} to give everything within 7m (corpses and thralls) to one burst. The more you give, the harder it hits. Pull the pack onto a pile of bodies first.

burst.title: Corpse Explosion
burst.body: <kbd>Right-click</kbd> a corpse to burst it under a pack. Best when the dead are already on you, or your legion is full.

hurt.title: Hurt?
hurt.body: Press Q (the Heal slot at the left edge) to drink a healing flask. T returns you to the Chapterhouse. Falling costs nothing but the walk back, and − on the Wave Speed dial eases the pressure.

elite.title: An elite
elite.body: Elites glow and carry an affix; read its tag in the target frame (top) before you engage. They drop soul shards, and five shards summon the Prelate.

surge.title: Grave Surge
surge.body: A crypt has cracked open. Kill most of what climbs out before it seals (about 20s) and it yields a guaranteed relic and bonus gold.

relic.title: A relic
relic.body: Loot goes to your Reliquary{p:I}. Equip gear there; the Workbench{p:C} turns ore and bars into more.

armor.title: Set armor
armor.body: Armor comes in five-piece sets, one look per discipline, and any class can wear any set. Open your Reliquary{p:I} and double-click a piece to wear it; it shows on your hero. Wear 2, 4 or 5 pieces of the same set to unlock set bonuses; hover a piece to see them. Later areas drop the rarer, stronger sets.

setBonus.title: A set bonus is awake
setBonus.body: Two pieces of the same armor set are worn, so its first set bonus is active. Hover any piece: green lines are on, grey lines need more pieces (4 and 5 are the big ones). A bag item marked completes in its arrow line will switch a bonus on. The Character sheet (J) shows what each set still needs and where it drops.

legendary.title: A legendary set
legendary.body: Legendary pieces are rare and change how you play. Each set is built for one discipline, and its pieces drop from area bosses (and very rarely from elites in the Cloister, Pyre and Fen); your own discipline’s set is the most likely. Wear 2, 4 or 5 pieces of the same set: two is a nudge, four changes a mechanic, five defines the build. Hover a piece for exactly what each tier does. Wearing four or more gives your hero a faint glow in the set’s colour. The Codex lists all four sets and where they drop.

affix.title: A rolled relic
affix.body: Gear now drops with an item level and up to three affixes, rolled by the server so nobody can edit them. More affixes means a richer colour; a higher item level means bigger numbers. Violet † lines feed your legion, essence and rites. Hover a piece: the arrow says if it beats what you wear. Salvage and selling pay more for good rolls.

gearEquip.title: Gear you can read
gearEquip.body: Hover or select a piece in the Reliquary{p:I} and every stat says what it does for you: VIT is health, INT is spell power and essence. A bag item wears a small green ▲ when it beats what you wear for your discipline, and a red ▼ when it is worse; hover it for why. Press J to see which stats to look for.

atlas.title: The Gear Atlas
atlas.body: What is worth wearing, and where does it drop? The Gear Atlas [[(. key)||(in the Menu)]] lists every piece with its drop chances, how to craft it and a green ▲ or red ▼ against what you wear. Best for me shows your top upgrades.

statSheet.title: Your Character sheet
statSheet.body: At the top: what you are looking for, the stats and weapons that suit your discipline and the slots most worth fixing. Below: every number your hero fights with. Click a line to see where it comes from. The Set bonuses block lists what your armor sets give and which piece completes the next one.

necroWeapon.title: A weapon that changes your left click
necroWeapon.body: Necromancer weapons change your Bone Needle (left click): a Scythe becomes a close reaping arc that pays a soul per kill, a Wand casts faster but softer, a Ritual Sickle leaves targets Withered, and a Staff reaches farther and pierces. Off-hands add a passive. Hover any piece in the Reliquary{p:I} for its line; the Codex{p:K} lists them all.

codex.title: The Codex
codex.body: Press <kbd>K</kbd> for everything you have met: every rite, every kind of dead, and how to beat it.

signature.title: Your signature rite awakens
signature.body: Level 10: [[press <kbd>R</kbd> for your class's own rite. Hover the new slot||tap the new slot on your hotbar for your class's own rite. Press and hold it]] to read what it does.{auto} On Easy, Auto may also use it when the fight calls for it.{/auto}

ascend.title: The Altar of Ascension stirs
ascend.body: The Prelate has fallen. At the Altar in the Chapterhouse you may Ascend: your Damage and Wave Speed tiers reset, but your seals, soul shards, level, gold and relics stay, and you earn Ashes for permanent boons. The hotter the vows you swore, the more Ashes.

souls.title: Soul Harvest
souls.body: The skull above your hotbar is full. Your next Marrow Spear, Miasma Circle or Black Litany is free and 50% larger; the empowered slots glow jade.

sanctify.title: Sanctified
sanctify.body: That pale gold halo is a Deacon's blessing: the enemy takes 30% less damage while it lasts. Kill the Deacon, or turn your rites on something else until it fades.

altar_unlocks.title: Shards open new vows and boons
altar_unlocks.body: You carry enough soul shards to open something new at the Altar of Ascension in the Chapterhouse: a harder vow or a Covenant boon that changes how you play. Keep 5 shards back for the Sundered Bell.

vows.title: Swear a vow
vows.body: At the Altar of Ascension you may swear Vows: curses you choose, like older dead, no healing flasks or a tougher Prelate. Each carries heat, and the hotter your run, the more Ashes it pays when the Prelate falls. Seals never close again: the vows are your difficulty. Changing them mid-run restarts the run's tally.

boons.title: Ashes to spend
boons.body: Your Ashes buy permanent Covenant Boons at the Altar of Ascension: more health, cheaper upgrades, and boons that change how you play, like a thrall at your side on arrival or corpses that last longer. Soul shards unlock the stranger ones.

prelate.title: Five soul shards
prelate.body: Enough to wake the Bell-Sworn Prelate. Offer them at the Sundered Bell in the Bell Sanctum, and learn to step out of its bronze rings.

grimoire.title: The Grimoire
grimoire.body: New rites have come to you. [[Click||Tap]] the swap arrows below a hotbar spell[[ (or press L)||, or open the Grimoire from the Menu,]] to choose which unlocked rites sit on [[slots 1–5; slot 5 also uses right-click||slots 1–5]]. Your signature stays on [[R||the sixth slot]]. Each rite keeps its cooldown.

rite_skull.title: Wailing Skull
rite_skull.body: The skull hunts the enemy nearest your cursor, then leaps on to two more, each bite a little weaker. Finish a wounded foe with it and it earns an extra leap. Good for elites and stragglers.

rite_step.title: Grave Step
rite_step.body: Aim at a corpse up to 12m away to re-form on it in blood mist, bleeding everything beside it. The body stays, so follow with Corpse Explosion or Exhume. It never carries you through a sealed door.

rite_frost.title: Grave Frost
rite_frost.body: A cone of grave cold: everything it touches is Chilled, slower to move and to strike. Breathe on the same pack again and the Chilled enemies shatter for +50% damage.

procession.title: A procession
procession.body: Not every wave is a mix. Now and then the dead arrive as a procession, a themed band named on the banner (hounds and rats, a choir, a censer and its bells). Read the name, then pick your rites for it.

censer.title: Censer Bearer
censer.body: Its bronze incense Incenses the dead around it: faster feet, faster blows (bronze motes on them). Kill the censer first and the pack slows back down.

wraith.title: Choir Wraith
wraith.body: Pale song-lines mark a ring where you stand; when the hymn breaks, the ring screams. One step out is enough. Wraiths leave no corpse.

swarm.title: Skull-rats
swarm.body: They pour out in packs and leave no corpses. Needles are wasted on them: a Miasma, a Grave Frost cone or a Corpse Explosion ends a whole pack at once.

golem.title: Bone Golem
golem.body: A slow giant with a wide bronze-brown slam ring: step out, then punish it. It falls apart into three corpses, a whole legion or a Litany in one kill.

gargoyle.title: Belfry Gargoyle
gargoyle.body: When a bronze circle fills in under you, a gargoyle is about to dive onto it. Walk out, then turn on it: it sits grounded in the rubble for a moment after it lands. A stun knocks it out of the air.

moth.title: Shroud Moth
moth.body: An ochre ring means grave dust is coming down. Step out before it bursts, and stay out of the cloud it leaves for a few seconds. Moths are fragile: one or two good hits.

bats.title: Tithe Bats
bats.body: They bite and flit away, again and again, and leave no corpses. Don't chase them. Hold your ground and sweep the flock with Miasma, a Grave Frost cone or Bone Mantle.

seraph.title: Weeping Seraph
seraph.body: It blesses every ally near it at once (priest-gold motes: they take less damage). Kill the seraph first, or silence it with a Dirge.

boss_gravedigger.title: The King's Grave
boss_gravedigger.body: Offer 2 soul shards here to wake the Gravedigger King. When a grave outline opens under you, step off it or be Buried (rooted, casting allowed). In his last phase, stay out of the open pits.

boss_abbess.title: The Abbess's Reliquary
boss_abbess.body: Offer 3 soul shards to wake the Bone Abbess. Break her four skull niches first: they heal her and each one broken tears at her. Stand between the chorus spokes, and spend the corpses before her Communion eats them.

boss_congregation.title: The Drowned Font
boss_congregation.body: Offer 4 soul shards to wake the Drowned Congregation. When the tide crests march out, put a pew between you and her: it is the only cover from the Flood Hymn. The rising water slows you off her dais.

boss_saint.title: The Saint's Litter
boss_saint.body: Offer 5 soul shards to wake the Plague Saint. She grows as strong as you. Her Rot Rain leaves rot pools, and she heals while she stands in one: pull her out onto clean ground before you unload. Later her Plague Doctors feed her through a green link: kill them first.

boss_regent.title: The Ember Altar
boss_regent.body: Offer 6 soul shards to wake the Cinder Regent. He grows as strong as you. When Conflagration begins the whole arena will burn: run to a grey ash circle and stay on it. Kill the Pyre Priests early, before their coals cover the ash.

plague_doctor.title: Plague Doctor
plague_doctor.body: A green ring means a plague flask is coming. Step out, then stay off the rot pool it leaves behind.

flagellant.title: Flagellant
flagellant.body: Wounded below half, a Flagellant frenzies (blood motes): much faster feet and blows. Take it from half to dead in one burst.

cloister.title: The Plague Cloister
cloister.body: The blight grows with you: the dead here always match the highest-level player inside (never below 20), so every kill is worth your level. The Plague Saint waits at the Saint’s Litter.

omen.title: The Week’s Omen
omen.body: One omen hangs over the diocese each week (the icon on the left, hover it for the rules), the same for everyone: Blood Moon (more elites), Drowned Week (bigger waves) or The Tolling (Bell-Tolled elites, double shards). It changes on Monday, UTC.

chain.title: Kill Chain
chain.body: Kills that land within 4 seconds of each other build a chain. Every tier (5, 12, 25, 45, 80) adds a bonus to XP and gold, and the count turns warmer. Keep killing to keep it; dying ends it.

pyre.title: The Cinder Pyre
pyre.body: Fire, ash and embers. The dead here are level-scaled like the Cloister’s (never below 30) and every one of them leaves burning ground: orange rings are coals about to land, glowing cracks are ground to leave.

warren.title: The Catacomb Warren
warren.body: Nine chambers split by tall half-walls. Walls stop cones and blows, so break line of sight to a caster by stepping behind one, and fight in the gaps where the swarm has to funnel.

wing.title: The Alchemist's Wing
wing.body: A safe workshop for brewing. Click the Great Cauldron (or the Alembic) to brew flasks, tonics and elixirs, and the Reagent Shelf to see every herb, reagent and ichor you have found. Today's brew of the day gives one extra the first time you make it. Drink with Z (elixir) and X (tonic).

coliseum.title: The Bone Coliseum
coliseum.body: A pit with four gates and fast surges: twice the elites, richer drops. Fight from the pillar islands, and clear each surge before the next arrives.

cinder_husk.title: Cinder Husk
cinder_husk.body: When a Husk falls it bursts into embers and leaves burning ground where it died. Finish it at range, or step back the moment it drops.

pyre_priest.title: Pyre Priest
pyre_priest.body: An orange ring means a coal is coming. Step out, then stay off the burning ground it leaves behind.

cinderhound.title: Cinderhound
cinderhound.body: Burning hounds that hunt in packs of two or three and flank fast. Fight with your back to a wall or a Bone Ward; their corpses rise as hounds of your own.

fen.title: The Mourning Fen
fen.body: A drowned marsh, level-scaled like the Pyre (never below 45). Bog water slows you; the pale-rimmed hummocks are dry and safe, so fight from them. The Bog Hag’s magenta ring hexes your thralls (30% softer for six seconds): kill her first or move your legion out of it.

bog_hag.title: Bog Hag
bog_hag.body: A magenta ring on your thralls is her hex: anything inside deals 30% less damage for six seconds. Kill her first, or pull the legion out before the ring fills.

mire_leech.title: Mire Leech
mire_leech.body: They come in swarms of four to six and leave no corpse. Sweep them with Miasma or another area rite instead of chasing them one by one.

fen_wisp.title: Fen Wisp
fen_wisp.body: A teal ring under your feet is a cold pulse that slows you. Step out, and do not chase it: it backs away toward the open water, where you wade slowly.

drowned_sexton.title: Drowned Sexton
drowned_sexton.body: A rust-brown line is his grave-hook: it drags you toward him, then the slam follows. Step off the line, or cross it on a hummock and be ready to leave the slam ring.

boss_mire.title: The Mire Altar
boss_mire.body: Offer 7 soul shards to wake the Mire Mother. She sinks and resurfaces under a hummock (a ring marks it: leave, then hit her while she is winded); phase 2 floods the marsh; in phase 3 she raises every corpse in the Fen, so spend yours first.

slag_brute.title: Slag Brute
slag_brute.body: A slow slam that cracks a wide ring and leaves it burning. Leave the ring when it winds up, and do not fight standing in the old one.

meal.title: Well fed
meal.body: A cooked meal heals over time and stacks with a flask. Cook fish at the Cooking Fire in the Acre; the rarer the fish, the bigger the meal. One meal at a time.

belt.title: Your belt
belt.body: The Belt at the left edge holds Heal (Q), Elixir (Z) and Tonic (X). Healing flasks fill Heal by themselves. For the other two, click an empty slot to pick a brew from your bag, or drag one onto it from the Reliquary (I); the Put on belt button on a brew does the same. Hover any slot to read what it does.

brew.title: Elixirs and tonics
brew.body: You can hold one elixir (combat: damage, wards) and one tonic (utility: speed) at once. A new elixir replaces the old one; the same brew again extends it. Click a belt slot (or use Put on belt in the Reliquary) to choose which brew it holds, then press Z for your elixir and X for your tonic. The belt at the left edge shows both slots and their timers.

reagent.title: Reagents
reagent.body: Grave Dust, ectoplasm, bile, ash and boss ichor are Alchemy reagents. Take them to the Alchemist's Wing (the Chapterhouse's east door): four Grave Dust brew a tonic at level 1, no garden needed. Better reagents make better elixirs as your Alchemy rises; every brew is an Elixir or a Tonic you drink with Z or X.

tool.title: Gathering tools
tool.body: Carry a tool and it speeds that skill up: +5% success per metal tier (the best one you carry counts). Forge hatchets, pickaxes, rods and spades at the Bone Kiln (Tools tab) or the Workbench. Put them on the tool belt under the paper doll in the Reliquary{p:I} and they stop taking bag space.

toolBelt.title: The tool belt
toolBelt.body: Four belt slots hold one tool each: hatchet, pickaxe, rod and spade. A belted tool counts for gathering exactly like one in your bag (the best of both wins) and takes no bag space. Select a tool and press Put on belt, or double-click it; double-click it on the belt to take it off, which needs a free bag slot. Skills{p:P} shows which tool each skill is using.

legion.title: Spare gear for your legion
legion.body: That weapon or armor can arm your thralls instead of being salvaged. Open the Legion tab beside the Grimoire (Y, or the button in the Reliquary): one Weapon and one Armour slot, kept outside your bag. Its stats become thrall damage, health and attack speed, and each spare piece shows ▲ or ▼ against what the legion wears. Spend gold there to Reinforce the bindings: it strengthens the thralls you have standing at once. A swapped piece reaches the thralls you raise next.

rune.title: A Relic rune
rune.body: Runes change how a rite behaves, not how hard it hits: one turns five corpses into a single giant, another delays Black Litany and doubles it. Open the Grimoire{p:L}, choose a rite and socket the rune under the bar. One rune per rite, and it fits only its own. Take it out whenever you like; it is never lost. Runes stack in the Reliquary, can rest in the Vault and can be ground at the Bone Grinder. The Codex{p:K} lists them all.

runeHunt.title: Where runes come from
runeHunt.body: Every necromancer rite already has a socket in the Grimoire{p:L}: what you hunt for is the Relic runes to fill them. Elites shed one about once in ten to twenty (more often in the deeper grounds), a Grave Surge offering is a rune about a third of the time, every boss leaves one on its first kill, and chests in the Catacomb Depths often hold one. The Gear Atlas (.) and the Codex{p:K} list each rune and where it drops.

runeSocketed.title: The rune is set
runeSocketed.body: The rite now wears the rune: a jade badge sits on its slot, and hovering the slot shows exactly what changed and what it costs. Swap runes in the Grimoire{p:L} to try another style; your cooldowns are not reset.

loadouts.title: Save a loadout
loadouts.body: Tired of re-placing rites, runes and your weapon by hand? Set the build you like, open the Grimoire{p:L} and press Save what I have now under the bar. A loadout keeps your five rites, the rune in each rite and your weapon and off-hand together; Apply puts them all back at once. You can keep six, and in Settings (Esc) you can give Next loadout and Loadout 1-6 a key of your choice (they start unbound). A piece you have since sold or stored in the Vault is skipped and named, and nothing is ever lost from a full bag.

depths.title: A stair in the dark
depths.body: The Warren's west chamber hides a stair down to the Catacomb Depths: floor after floor of small chambers, each a level older than the last. Click the glowing stair to go down; once you have been deeper than the first floor it asks whether to start at depth 1 or resume at your deepest floor. Slay a floor's quota and the stair beyond it opens; leaving or falling ends the run, and whatever you looted is yours. Your legion comes with you. Solo for now.

depths_floor.title: Slay, then descend
depths_floor.body: The count at the top (and under the minimap) is this floor's quota. When it is met the stair down glows, the minimap points to it and the dead stop coming: Click it to go deeper. The way back up is behind you; it ends the run, so it asks twice. The dead come through the doorways to find you, so fight in the gaps and use the walls: they stop cones and blows.

depths_affix.title: Elites with company
depths_affix.body: From depth 5 an elite carries more than one affix, one more every fifth floor, and all of them work at once. The target frame names them all. Burst a Shrouded one inside your Miasma, step out of Bell-Tolled rings, spend corpses before a Hungering one eats them, and keep your distance from a Vengeful one's Risen.

depths_chest.title: The fifth floor's chest
depths_chest.body: Every fifth floor holds a chest in a side chamber, marked on the minimap. It gives gear with at least one affix, finds from the depth's own ground, gold and experience, and now and then a Relic rune. The deeper the chest, the more it holds.

depths_solo.title: A descent for one
depths_solo.body: Friends can share a world, but a descent is a solo run. When you take the stair from a party you step out of it automatically, go down alone, and rejoin your party when the run ends. Shared floors are on the list.

ghoul.title: Barrow Ghoul
ghoul.body: Barrow Ghouls tunnel toward you. When the ground cracks in a ring, step out of it, then kill the ghoul before it digs back down.

acolyte.title: Lich Acolyte
acolyte.body: A Lich Acolyte turns your fallen thralls against you. Kill it first, or keep your legion out of its crimson ring. Sacrificing a thrall (Litany) is safe.

templar.title: Bell-Sworn Templar
templar.body: Blows from the front glance off its bronze shield. Come at it from the side, let your thralls turn it, or Fracture it (Marrow Spear, Ivory Cleave) to break the guard.

acre.title: The Sexton's Acre
acre.body: No waves ever come here. Click a tree, an ore seam, a fishing spot on the pond or a burial plot, and your necromancer keeps working it until it is spent. Coffin-Oaks just north of the entrance, the nearby Copper Seam and Pauper’s Grave, and Still Pools on the pond are usable at level 1. The stronger nodes lie further from the door. Press P to see your skills.

laborers_working.title: Your laborers at work
laborers_working.body: The dead you sent to work (<kbd>H</kbd>) stand at their posts in the Acre: chopping, mining, digging or fishing. A gold check over one means it has finished work for you to collect. <kbd>Hover</kbd> a laborer to see its post and time, or <kbd>click</kbd> it to open the Laborers.

gather.title: Working a node
gather.body: Each swing, cast or dig is one work cycle; the ring under you fills as it goes. Every success gives skill XP and a find. For hands-off work in the Acre, open P, choose a node and Start AFK. Keep the game open: your hero changes nodes and waits for respawns until your bag fills. Skills can stay open; moving, casting or other panels pause work. Pause AFK stops it whenever you like.

bag_full.title: Your bag is full
bag_full.body: Nothing more fits: gathering stops and loot stays on the ground until you free a slot. Sell junk in the Reliquary{p:I}, move materials to the Vault (<kbd>V</kbd>), or grind spare gear at the Bone Grinder in the Acre.

skill_up.title: A skill rises
skill_up.body: Each level improves your odds on every node of that skill and opens a stronger one. The Skills panel{p:P} shows what the next level unlocks and your total level.

rich_node.title: A rich node
rich_node.body: Gold-lit nodes in the hunting grounds hold more before they are spent and come back twice as fast. Taking a hit stops gathering, so clear the dead around it first.

bag_filling.title: Your Reliquary is filling
bag_filling.body: Make room before it fills: the Vault (V, in the Chapterhouse or the Acre) keeps materials and gear for every character on this account, and the Bone Grinder in the Acre turns spare gear into ingots, planks and reagents. In the Reliquary{p:I}, Sell all junk clears common and uncommon gear, and the padlock keeps an item out of every bulk button.

vault.title: The Ossuary Vault
vault.body: One stash of 120 slots, shared by all your characters. Click an item to move its whole stack across; Deposit materials, Deposit all, Take materials, Take all and Sort do it in bulk, and locked items always stay in your bag. It opens with V in the Chapterhouse or the Acre, and a move that will not fit changes nothing.

salvage.title: Salvaging
salvage.body: The Bone Grinder breaks unwanted gear into ingots (or planks from staffs, wands and grimoires) by rarity, plus Grave Dust and other reagents, and trains Salvaging. If the yield will not fit your bag, nothing is ground. Worn and locked gear is never touched.

reforge.title: Reforge a roll
reforge.body: At the Workbench{p:C}, the Reforge tab re-rolls one affix of a piece you carry or wear. The affix stays; its number is drawn again, anywhere in the range its item level allows, for gold. The price is shown before you confirm and rises about 25% with every reforge of the same piece. It can come out lower, and a roll already at the top of its range cannot be reforged, so spend on the weak lines.

boss_seal.title: A Covenant Seal at the altar
boss_seal.body: Click a boss altar with a Covenant Seal in your bag to call an Empowered boss: more health and harder hits, with a red-gold glow, for a Seal and gold. Its kill pays one guaranteed epic-or-better piece with much better odds of a legendary. A fight you lose can be tried again free. Seals turn up when you dig Crypt Collapses and the Barrow-King's Tomb or fish the Abyssal Coelacanth.

people.title: People of the Covenant
people.body: Some of the Covenant still stand in these halls: the Prior in the Chapterhouse, the Sexton in the Acre, the Apothecary at her counter in the Alchemist’s Wing (the Chapterhouse’s east door). Click one, or stand close and press E. A gold ! means they have something new to say. They only advise. The Next line under the minimap shows one suggestion; Settings can hide it.

station.title: A working station
station.body: Stations turn what you gather into something useful. The Sawpit’s warm gold light marks where to click for wood recipes. Recipes need the matching skill level and their ingredients in your bag; crafting grants skill XP too. The server checks every recipe, and its reason is shown if one fails.

rite_fan.title: Bone Fan
rite_fan.body: Your left click now throws three slivers, each at a different enemy near the one you click. It clears packs fast but is weaker on one target (the Prelate only ever takes one sliver). Swap back to Bone Needle on the Grimoire's LMB socket for bosses.

rite_lance.title: Rot Lance
rite_lance.body: Your left click now pierces the first two enemies in line and leaves Withered ticking on each. Line the dead up; the rot keeps working while you move on.

rite_offering.title: Grave Offering
rite_offering.body: Press {key:grave_offering} on a corpse to burn it into Grave Essence and a little health. Spend the bodies you won't raise: when your legion is full, or when essence runs dry.

rite_cleave.title: Ivory Cleave
rite_cleave.body: Press {key:ivory_cleave} to sweep a bone crescent through everything in a wide arc in front of you, Fracturing it. Cleave the pack that reaches you, then Spear the line.

rite_veil.title: Veil Step
rite_veil.body: Press {key:veil_step} to slip a few metres toward the cursor, no corpse needed. It stops at walls and sealed doors. Use it to leave a cone or a bell ring; auto combat never casts it (it only walks out of boss telegraphs and pools).

rite_rally.title: Rally the Dead
rite_rally.body: With thralls at your side, press {key:rally_dead} with the cursor on the enemy you want dead: your legion heals, hits harder and faster, and turns on it. The jade sigils show who is rallied.

rite_seed.title: Carrion Seed
rite_seed.body: Press {key:carrion_seed} on a corpse in the pack's path. The bud arms in a moment, then bursts in rot when an enemy comes close. One seed at a time; if another rite uses that corpse, the seed goes with it.

rite_siphon.title: Soul Siphon
rite_siphon.body: Latch the jade tether onto something sturdy and keep moving: it follows the target for 3 seconds, draining it into your health and essence. It snaps if they get too far away.

rite_prison.title: Bone Prison
rite_prison.body: Drop the cage on a pack as it closes. Everything inside is rooted for a moment and Fractured: the perfect setup for a Marrow Spear or a Corpse Explosion. Rooted enemies still swing at whatever stands beside them.

rite_hands.title: Grave Hands
rite_hands.body: Cast it where the dead lie thickest: every corpse in the field adds more hands and more damage, and none are used up. Everything inside is slowed while the hands claw.

rite_storm.title: Bone Storm
rite_storm.body: Start the storm on a pile of corpses to make it last longer (they are not used up), then let it drift through the pack on its own while you keep casting.

rite_mantle.title: Bone Mantle
rite_mantle.body: Cast it standing among the dead: each corpse within 6m thickens a barrier that holds for 6 seconds, while whirling shards cut whatever reaches you. With no corpses you still get a thin mantle.
